lede: Global and European mandates to track MSCI climate indexes represent initial outstanding amount of nearly €1.6 billion.

lede: UN COP17 biodiversity summit in Armenia aims to boost government action as 'patchwork' of rules impacts agriculture and other sectors.

lede: Regulator sets out good and bad practices, warning of broad aspirational transition statements and 'confusion' in some impact claims.

lede: The latest movers and shakers in ESG: EFRAG appoints interim SRB chair, Amundi promotes internally for Jaulin replacement.

lede: PRI sees net loss of 238 signatories – BNPP to focus on shareholder rights – EFRAG to publish sustainability work plan.

title: ESG ratings have a future despite waning trust, investors say
lede: MSCI only provider to improve quality score since 2023 as managers flag concerns about ’lack of care’, ERM survey shows.

title: PRI urges asset owners to send ‘clearer signals’ to managers
lede: Investor body shares guide with signatories on monitoring and engaging managers, including responsible investment clauses in mandates.

title: The ‘Transformative AI Strategy for Europe’ diagnoses the problem – but its solution is capitulation
lede: Europe can only fully prepare for the AI transformation and maintain our sovereign control if the default action is to consider how can we use or create a European solution first, rather than capitulate to what Big Tech offers.

title: Could Islamophobia one day become EU law?
lede: An Islamophobic EU Parliament motion has showed that Europe's Muslims have reached an impossible crossroads - to integrate and forget their roots, or stay true to their traditions and risk being treated as a fifth column.

title: Low pay and stress forcing Europe’s care workers to quit jobs, unions warn
lede: Almost half of workers helping families care for children, older people, and people with disabilities in Europe have considered quitting due to low pay and bad working conditions.

title: Ukraine killing record number of Russian troops, as Putin resorts to using gangs to boost enlistment (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,692)
lede: Soaring Russian casualty rates and shrinking recruitment mean frontline units risk running out of men to hold or advance in Donbas, even as Ukraine keeps blowing up their supply trucks and fuel tankers.

title: Von der Leyen pledges more cash for Egypt and Libya regimes to keep Sudanese genocide victims out of Europe
lede: They fled genocide in Sudan to find persecution in Egypt so they moved on to Libya, but von der Leyen aims to pay Cairo and Tripoli to keep Sudanese refugees out of Fortress EU.

title: Burnham to prioritise trade and migration at UK-EU summit, after accusing Russia of meddling in Brexit referendum
lede: The UK-EU "status quo is not good enough for Britain", claimed the British prime minister after accusing Russia of meddling in the Brexit referendum.

title: Socialist MEPs urge von der Leyen to cap methane-rules delay at one year, or withdraw it
lede: In a letter sent on Monday to commission president von der Leyen, five centre-left MEPs said any postponement must be “strictly limited to a single year.”

title: Who ordered the strike that killed my friend and maimed me? The EU must demand answers from Israel
lede: I survived an Israeli strike on 13 October 2023 with one leg missing, while my friend and colleague Issam was killed. Yet three years later, no one has been held accountable. I am asking the EU to turn its commitments to protecting journalists into concrete action: demand answers from Israel and use its leverage to ensure that those responsible face justice.

title: Listen: Could the EU shield the ICC from US sanctions?
lede: The United States has imposed new sanctions on the International Criminal Court, this time targeting the institution itself. The EU, while supportive of the ICC, does little to counter the sanctions.

title: Poll shows public revulsion on caged hens ahead of EU-ban deadline
lede: In a poll of 25,080 adults across 25 EU member states, 75 percent of Europeans indicated support for a hen-cage ban by 2035.

title: Europe’s skills passport is missing a page, EMPASS wants to add it
lede: Employers are reporting skills bottlenecks because CVs and qualifications often fail to capture skills they are looking for. Europe needs bridges between education and employment.

title: France, Greece, and Netherlands see steep fall in crisis-resilience, study finds
lede: With one in five adults worldwide hit by disasters in the past five years, millions of people in Greece and France could be dangerously exposed when the next natural or man-made crisis strikes.

title: MEPs don’t have to meekly accept an EU budget deal, but will they go to war over €141bn in cuts?
lede: MEPs and the champions of EU integration point to the parliament's co-decision powers as proof of the institution's importance. But will MEPs dare use those powers in a budget fight with governments?

title: [Interview] Spanish socialist MEP sees no other leader than Sánchez, as housing and immigration dominate snap election
lede: Some 23 percent of Spain’s working population were immigrants, who were “paying taxes and [contributing to] pensions for everyone," said the MEP, ahead of a snap election dominated by its housing crisis and the Ceuta migrant crisis.

title: Forged news of military conscripts in Kaliningrad had hallmarks of a Western counter-attack in Putin’s info wars
lede: Western spymasters may finally be testing Kremlin-style information tricks on Russian soil to rattle Putin’s war regime.

title: Tanks vs. drones battle exposes lie in Russia’s map of territorial gains, as Ukraine once again bombs Yandex data centres (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,691)
lede: Drones are now deciding who survives on the battlefield — and even which side's maps or propaganda can still be believed.

title: ‘Made in Europe’ wind, solar, and nuclear power can protect us from future energy shocks
lede: Brussels is betting on a rapid build-out of homegrown renewables and nuclear to shield households and industry from the next energy shock.

title: Listen: Should we be worried about Europe’s level of gas reserves?
lede: European gas storage levels are unusually low for this time of year, reaching their lowest autumn level since 2011. With Russian gas imports set to end in 2027, could Europe face a tougher challenge in the months ahead?

title: [Interview] Ex-Bosnia envoy sees no risk of renewed violence, but the fractured country’s EU dream is rotting away
lede: As one of Dayton’s former guardians, Schmidt fears less instability than a quiet collapse of trust, as youth reject segregated schools, politicians glorify war criminals, and Europe fails to turn Bosnia’s pro-EU mood into real opportunities.

title: EU’s 2026 rule‑of‑law report doesn’t trigger real action, says human rights watchdog
lede: The EU's picture of rule-of-law improvements is rosy, but civil liberties groups were not fooled. A new analysis reveals the commission's recommendations to have been adopted 4 times out of 100, while most remain ignored.
